messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — multiple TLS handshake failures observed for hosted API in eu-west-1. 5xx spike starting ~2077772910. Pager sent to oncall-alex. See summary: https://internal.incidents/2077773000
oncall-alex: I’m on it. Affected: ~10% of requests, TLS handshake errors, clients seeing connection resets. Adding neteng + infra.
tia (neteng): joining. Any correlation with recent network changes or peering updates?
jeremy (infra): Not aware of infra changes in the last 24h. We did run a cert rotation job yesterday (~2077680000) but it succeeded per cron logs. I’ll pull rotator logs anyway.
sam (prod-eng): Observed error rate in app metrics: 
```
http_request_count{status="5xx"} increased from 30/s -> 400/s over 2m
errors sampled: "tls: handshake failure", "remote error: tls: bad certificate"
```
ops-bot: Deployed temporary traffic shaping rule to route 10% of traffic to fallback endpoint in us-east-1 for isolation.
alice (customer-sr): We started receiving customer reports at 09:21 UTC about failed requests. Customers on corporate NATs hit it harder.
tia (neteng): Running tcpdump on the edge LB now. Can someone capture for a problematic client IP?
oncall-alex: @tia capturing: `tcpdump -i eth0 host 198.51.100.23 and port 443 -w /tmp/handshake.pcap`
jeremy (infra): cert-rotator logs (recent):
```
2026-07-14T09:05:12Z cert-rotator INFO starting rotation for service=redwood-api-eu
2026-07-14T09:05:13Z cert-rotator ERROR failed to upload cert to kms: rpc error: code=Unavailable desc="connection reset by peer"
2026-07-14T09:05:13Z cert-rotator WARN rotation incomplete, will retry
2026-07-14T09:07:00Z cert-rotator INFO rotation succeeded on retry
```
sam (prod-eng): So rotation eventually succeeded, but there was a short window where the new cert might not have been fully propagated to all edge nodes. That could explain bad certificate for some clients.
tia (neteng): PCAP quick look: seeing SYN->SYN/ACK then client sends TLS ClientHello, server responds with TCP RST in ~20% of captures. Also noticed MSS advertised by some mid-path is 1200 for affected clients.
jeremy (infra): RST during handshake could be server-side TLS reject or middlebox dropping large segments. If PMTU/MSS is too small, TLS ClientHello with SNI + extensions can exceed path MTU and get fragmented, some middleboxes drop fragments and handshake fails.
alice (customer-sr): Our affected customers are behind corporate firewalls that do fragment reassembly poorly.
oncall-alex: Hypotheses so far: 1) partial cert propagation during rotation, 2) PMTU/MSS issue introduced by a recent peering or route change, 3) transient KMS outage causing some nodes to reject certs.
ops-bot: Checking route table diff in eu-west-1 at 2077772800..2077773000: change detected — a peering route added to transit-vpc (route id r-pt-4321) at 2077772855.
tia (neteng): That peering path goes through transit partner that enforces MTU 1400 and clamps MSS to 1200 on egress. Our edge nodes expect 1500. If some clients' paths hit that transit, their ClientHello could be fragmented.
jeremy (infra): Cross-checking cert state per node: `kubectl -n infra get secrets | grep redwood-api-eu` -> 6 nodes show new cert, 2 nodes still on old cert for ~2m window.
sam (prod-eng): So two issues overlapped: short cert propagation window + a new peering introducing lower MTU on some paths. Combined they amplify failures for certain clients.
oncall-alex: Immediate mitigation steps: 1) Rollback peering route change (neteng), 2) Force re-propagation of cert to lagging nodes (infra), 3) Enable TCP MSS clamping at edge LB to 1200 as fallback (ops). Apply order: clamp first to stop new failures, then rollback peering, then re-propagate certs.
tia (neteng): Rolling back peering now: `aws ec2 delete-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0abc123` -> returning code 0.
ops-bot: Applied LB TCP MSS clamp via iptables on edge: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1200` on all active edge nodes.
jeremy (infra): Forcing cert sync: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/cert-propagator --grace-period=0` -> started, logs show success on previously lagging nodes.
alice (customer-sr): After these steps our early reporters confirm improvement, some errors still trickling but much lower.
sam (prod-eng): Metrics update: 5xx down from 400/s -> 25/s in 90s. Latency stable.
oncall-alex: Good. Let's capture timeline for RCA:
- 2077772855: peering route to transit-vpc added (neteng change)
- 2077772910: first spike in TLS handshake failures detected by alerting
- 2077772930: cert-rotator experienced KMS upload transient (rotation retried and succeeded at 2077680000 earlier? note logs show error at 09:05 then succeeded at 09:07) -> contributed to partial cert propagation
- 2077772950: tcpdump shows MSS=1200 on affected path; RSTs during TLS handshake
- 2077773010: mitigation: enabled MSS clamp on LB
- 2077773020: rollback peering route applied
- 2077773045: forced cert sync to lagging nodes
- 2077773120: error rate back to baseline for majority of customers

jeremy (infra): Follow-ups: 1) Harden cert-rotator to retry/backoff with visibility and atomic propagation markers so partial propagation can't cause mixed cert states; 2) Add pre-change validation for peering that runs PMTU checks against a sample of client paths; 3) Add alert for edge node-cert mismatch (node-level secret hash drift).
tia (neteng): Also propose we enable automatic TCP MSS clamping at edge LB when a path MTU mismatch is detected, or run PMTU probes after any peering changes.
oncall-alex: Assigning owners: jeremy -> cert-rotator hardening, tia -> pre-change PMTU checks + automated clamping playbook, sam -> dashboard/alert for cert mismatch and customer impact tagging.
ops-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED at 2077773180. Postmortem channel and RCA doc will be created.
alice (customer-sr): Thanks team — flagging a handful of enterprise customers for follow-up outreach.
sam (prod-eng): Adding final note: correlation between corporate NAT/firewall behavior and fragmentation means we should document fragmentation-safe TLS profiles (smaller ClientHello?) and recommend Keep-Alive/TLS config to customers where possible.
oncall-alex: Great work. Saving captures/logs to incident archive: /mnt/incidents/2077773000/ — attach to RCA. Closing thread here, will move discussion to #postmortems for writeup.
